sentences.text: Shri Vivek Singh, learned Senior Advocate for the app  Shivendra Singh Rawat, learned counsel for the appellant.

Shri Sonal Gupta, learned Additional Advocate General  respondent/State.
 Shri Mohammed Imran Khan, learned counsel for the res  No.2.

Per: Justice Gajendra Singh  Heard on I.A No.8275/2024 which is first application   389 of the Cr.P.C, 1973 for suspension of execution of remain  sentence filed on behalf of sole appellant- Badal S/o Dinesh
The appellant/accused has been convicted and sentence

Conviction Sentence  Fine if deposited, Imprisonment  Section Act Imprisonment  details Fine  366 IPC 10 years R.I. 1,000/- 6 months add  376(3) IPC 20 years R.I. 1,000/- 6 months add  5(L)/6 IPC 20 years R.I. 1,000/- 6 months add  Facts in brief are that appellant has been convicted  dated 18.01.2024 passed in S.T. No.83/2023 by Special Judge, POCSO Act, Ratlam for kidnapping and committing penetrative sexual assault towards a child below the age of 16 years on the date of incident i.e. 29.05.2023 on the basis of D.O.B 1.06.2007.
2 CRA-2158-2024 This application is preferred on the ground that mother of the prosecution (PW-2) and father of the prosecution (PW-3) and prosecutrix (PW-5) has not supported the case of prosecution.
Prosecutrix was in company of the present appellant/accused for more than 20 days i.e. from 29.05.2023 to 19.06.2023.
Prosecutrix did not stated even in her statement recorded under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C regarding commission of any offence and the documents of age has not been properly proved.

sentences.text: Learned counsel appearing for the complainant/victim also did not opposed the application for suspension of sentence.
Learned Govt. Advocate for the respondent/State has opposed the application referring to age of prosecutrix below the age of 16 years and the DNA finger print report Ex.p/29.

Considering para 5 of PW-1, PW-2 & PW-3 regarding the age of prosecutrix, the statement of victim PW-5 recorded under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C on 28.06.2023, without commenting on merits of the case, we find it proper to extend the benefit of suspension of execution of remaining jail sentence of the appellant.

Accordingly, I.A No.8275/2024 is allowed and it is directed that subject to depositing fine amount, if not already deposited and on furnishing personal bond by the appellant in the sum of Rs.50,000/-
(Rupees Fifty Thousands Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned trial Court, the execution of custodial part of the jail sentence shall remain suspended, till the final disposal of this appeal.

The 3 CRA-2158-2024 appellant after being enlarged on bail, shall mark his presence before the Registry of this Court on 16.06.2025 and on all such subsequent dates as may be fixed by the Registry of this Court in this regard.
List for final hearing in due course.
